identity.trade: Reeds and baskets: Hollowmere cuts the mere's reeds for thatch and weaves baskets for every market from here to the capital.

greeting: Harbourmaster. I keep the tide book. The tide keeps me.
You will hear Hollowmere before you see it. Ask at the Hollowmere Reed Cutters.
rumour: The tide tables are off by a quarter hour. For a week. The water is learning new habits.
The shoals went deep a month early. The old fishers say the cold comes from below.
Lights drift over the mere after midnight. The reed-cutters do not follow them.

opinions.hanne_yoxall: Hanne is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.morning: Dawn tide. The boats are out.

dialogue.aside: Take something. Anything. No, a bigger something. I insist.

greeting: Rooms are clean. The beds are honest about their age.
Smell that? That is the sea. Or the fish. Hard to say.
rumour: The fishers come in at dawn and drink till noon. Their wives come at one.
Somebody paid in old coin last night. Very old. Nobody knew the king on it.
The tide marks on the pier are wrong. Higher than last year, higher than the old stone.
Folk say Hollowmere was founded by someone who wanted to be left alone. We have not forgotten.

opinions.yarrow_tolliver: Yarrow undercuts me. I forgive Yarrow. Mostly.

time.evening: Boats are in. The catch is salted. Supper is fish.

dialogue.aside: I do not say this often. It is good to see a face I do not need to avoid.

greeting: Bring iron or bring coin. Preferably iron.
Hollowmere is reeds and baskets. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Hooks, gaffs and anchors. If it holds a boat, I forged it.
Good steel is dear. Bad steel is dearer, the day it breaks.
The gulls leave the harbour every evening in a line. They did not use to.

opinions.fenn_rawlin: Fenn has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Fenn.

time.night: Night tide. Quiet water, loud thoughts.

dialogue.aside: My friend. Come, I kept something for you. A small thing. It means a lot to me.

greeting: Everything has a price. Some of it is even written down.
First time in Hollowmere? The Hollowmere Reed Cutters is the place to start.
rumour: Hooks, floats and twine. If it is thin and sharp, it is a bestseller.
Folk buy more than they need, then bring half back. Fear shops strangely.
A boy swore he saw a ship at the mouth of the bay with no mast and no crew. The tide took it.
The Hollowmere Reed Cutters drew a stranger last month. He asked questions and bought nothing.

opinions.sunniva_swale: Sunniva lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.rain: Rain on the water. The fish bite better and so do the midges.

dialogue.aside: You have a new scar, and fewer coins than last time. Sit.

greeting: Come closer. My ears are old and your voice is young.
If it floats, I have fished from it. If it sank, I have fished it up.
rumour: Winters were colder, summers longer, and the wolves stayed home. Or so I choose to remember.
Fish tasted of iron last week. Not bad. Not right.
An old woman talks to the mere and says it answers.

opinions.merrin_larkspur: Merrin keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.morning: Dawn tide. The boats are out.

dialogue.aside: Tell me everything. No, truly. I will not ask twice. I will ask three times.

greeting: Cut low, cut clean, cut early. Cut late and the toads win.
Strangers in Hollowmere get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: I found a boardwalk plank snapped from underneath. Not worn. Pushed.
A net came up with a coil of old chain in it, links as long as a forearm. We put it back.

opinions.hadley_heron: Hadley knows the trade. I will say that for Hadley.
opinions.milo_ledger: Milo works hard and talks harder.

time.evening: Boats are in. The catch is salted. Supper is fish.

dialogue.aside: Up before dawn, friend? Then you saw the best of the day. I saw it first.

greeting: Mind your fingers. The reed bites back.
Welcome to Hollowmere. Mind the Hollowmere Reed Cutters. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: A basket came back full of feathers, no bird in sight. Not mine, not anyone's.
A seal followed my boat for a mile and spoke. I did not answer.
Baskets from here are said to keep bread fresh a week.

opinions.hanne_yoxall: Hanne works hard and talks harder.
opinions.milo_ledger: Milo knows the trade. I will say that for Milo.

time.night: Night tide. Quiet water, loud thoughts.

dialogue.aside: Take your time, friend. I am in no hurry. I am, in fact, very good at waiting.

greeting: Lines down by first light, or do not bother.
Folk come to Hollowmere for reeds and baskets. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: A light on the water last night, low, moving against the current. Nobody was out.
A boat came back empty with its sail torn, as if something had pulled at it.
A stranger asked at the Hollowmere Reed Cutters for the oldest person in Hollowmere. We sent him to the wrong house, on purpose.

opinions.bede_garland: Bede keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.
opinions.milo_ledger: Milo works hard and talks harder.

time.rain: Rain on the water. The fish bite better and so do the midges.

dialogue.aside: Ha! Friend! Pull up a stool, I have a story and half a loaf.

greeting: Hold the line. Not that way. Over, under, over.
Tide waits for nobody, and neither does a net.
rumour: Rope is dear and getting dearer. Cut a net, you cut a wage.
Tides follow the moon, they say. Ours follow something else. The old men have stopped betting.

opinions.bede_garland: Bede works hard and talks harder.
opinions.hadley_heron: Hadley knows the trade. I will say that for Hadley.

time.morning: Dawn tide. The boats are out.

dialogue.aside: Friend. Gently, now. Sit. I will make something warm.

greeting: Pitch, plank and promises. In that order.
Hollowmere is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: Somebody asked me for a boat with no name. I built it. I did not ask.
A light under the water off the point moves against the current.
The Hollowmere Reed Cutters was busy last week. Something is stirring, or somebody is.

opinions.cecily_fletcher: Cecily works hard and talks harder.
opinions.larkin_overton: Larkin knows the trade. I will say that for Larkin.

time.evening: Boats are in. The catch is salted. Supper is fish.

dialogue.aside: Hmph. You again. Fine. Sit. I did not say I was glad.

greeting: A pinch of this keeps meat for a month. A pinch of me keeps you out of my pans.
The Hollowmere Reed Cutters is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: Pans ran short this month. Somebody is selling our salt as theirs.
Ask anyone in Hollowmere about the Hollowmere Reed Cutters. You will get four stories and one fact.

opinions.cecily_fletcher: Cecily keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.night: Night tide. Quiet water, loud thoughts.

greeting: Hold the mule. He is not as bad as he looks.
rumour: Fewer carts on the road, more trouble at the verge.
If trade slows, Hollowmere feels it first. If it speeds up, Hollowmere feels it last.

opinions.hadley_heron: Hadley knows the trade. I will say that for Hadley.
opinions.hanne_yoxall: Hanne lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.rain: Rain on the water. The fish bite better and so do the midges.

dialogue.aside: Eh? Oh, it is you. I heard that. I always hear friends.

clues.note: A sack by the racks, crusted white, slit and loosely tied.
Wet prints, bare feet, from the water to the sheds and back.
A net cut clean, not torn. The cut edge is still wet.

stashes.say: You heave two sacks of salt from the pan shed.
